title: Why Cinema Popcorn Costs $9 (look demo)
request: Demo of The Fine Print's explainer look (look 4): every graphic building up step by step, sample numbers

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Why does a bucket of cinema popcorn cost nine dollars?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Almost everyone has paid it, and almost nobody asks why.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The corn costs about thirty five cents, the bucket forty five, and the butter fifty five.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That is one dollar and thirty five cents of real cost.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the cinema keeps the rest, seven dollars and sixty five cents.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your ticket money goes the other way, mostly to the film studio.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The studio can take more than half of every ticket in the first weeks of a new film.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the cinema earns more from one bucket than from one ticket.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That is why you walk past the snack counter before you reach your seat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And every one of us in the queue pays it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is the same at airports, stadiums and theme parks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next time, share one bucket, and it costs you four fifty.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Or eat before you go, and it costs you nothing.

sources: Sample numbers for a look demo of The Fine Print, made on 2026-10-15. Not a video to post: a real video takes every price and share from a saved source.
